articles.title: Barcelona move clear at the top after Fermín López’s double stuns Atlético Madrid
articles.summary: They had been in a battle, they had been behind and they had been on edge, but Barcelona found a way through, holding on to their place at the top of the table and holding the doubts at bay for another day.
body: At a noisy, intense Metropolitano, against an even more intense Atlético, they went behind to a Giuliano Simeone goal and for a while in a frantic first half it looked like there may be no way back. But they found it, two goals from Fermín López either side of half-time leading them to the kind of victory that brings a reward beyond just the points. It had been a long night, but they had made it.

Atlético flew into this, fuelled by the noise. They did more inside three minutes than in 90 against Bayern Munich in midweek. A superb clearance from Pau Cubarsí kept them at bay in the first minute. Álex Baena curled wide in the second. And they forced a corner in the third. Barcelona were overwhelmed and exposed, unable to settle, and Diego Simeone’s side could sense it.

articles.title: Crystal Palace poised to sack Pierre Sage and target Frank after Liverpool defeat
articles.summary: Frenchman under pressure after four successive defeats. Former Spurs manager Frank emerging as main candidate. Crystal Palace are poised to sack Pierre Sage after Sunday’s defeat by Liverpool left them bottom of the Premier League for the first time since December 2017, with Thomas Frank emerging…
body: The Frenchman, appointed in mid-June to replace Oliver Glasner, has been under mounting pressure since a 5-0 defeat by Brighton last month. There have been few signs of improvement as Palace have slumped to four successive league defeats.

Sage has guided Palace to only two wins from their 10 Premier League games this season and they have the league’s worst defensive record, with 24 goals conceded so far. Although there were promising moments during the 3-1 defeat by Liverpool at Selhurst Park on Sunday, their habit of conceding goals from set pieces has not been rectified and it is understood the patience of the club’s hierarchy has worn thin despite Sage only being at the helm for 16 matches.

He is expected to become the first Premier League manager to be sacked this season on Monday. Palace are already believed to have started the process of bringing in his replacement. Frank, who was dismissed by Tottenham in February, spoke to Palace in the summer and is said to be keen for a new challenge after a successful spell at Brentford.

articles.title: 'Not many sports teams have done it' - Wolff 'proud' of Mercedes turnaround
articles.summary: Toto Wolff says he's "proud" of Mercedes' turnaround to win the 2026 Formula 1 Constructors' Championship and feels very few sports teams have bounced back so quickly.
body: Mercedes won their ninth constructors' title on Sunday at the Sao Paulo Grand Prix, five years after their last championship, which was their eighth in a row at the time.

Regulation changes in 2022 ended Mercedes' dominance as they struggled to get on top of the so-called ground effect cars, but they have won the first season of the new 2026 cars, and also wrapped up the Drivers' Championship earlier this month with Kimi Antonelli.
"The thing is when you are in these difficult moments, like we all are sometimes in our lives, it's not that easy to keep going," said Wolff.
"Looking back in retrospect, you're saying, 'we needed these tough moments in order to grow as people or to grow as an organisation'. But when you're down, that is quite difficult to feel.

articles.title: NWSL playoffs: Gotham sneak into semi-finals despite zero shots on goal
articles.summary: Shield winners defeat Seattle Reign 1-0. Seattle own goal by Jordyn Bugg is the decider. Spirit and Thorns face off in other quarter-final. Ann-Katrin Berger made three saves and top-seeded Gotham FC ⁠protected a one-goal lead for most of the game, ⁠defeating the ⁠eighth-seeded ​Seattle Reign 1-0…
body: Gotham got on the board in the fourth minute on ⁠an own goal credited to Seattle’s Jordyn Bugg. ​Jaedyn Shaw ‌sent a corner ‌kick toward the near post and Bugg ‌misplayed it, sending it straight past her goalkeeper, Claudia Dickey.
The Shield winners took five shots during the game, but none of them were on target. They had 54% of possession but just 0.16 expected goals (xG) and zero big chances created.
Berger made one save in the first half and two more after half-time. One of the best goalkeepers in the sport, Berger led the league with a 0.85 ⁠goals-against average this season.

Seattle appeared to equalize in the 59th minute when veteran Reign midfielder Jess Fishlock found Nérilia Mondésir in the box. Mondésir finished past Berger, but the goal was ruled out because Fishlock was offside when Maddie Mercado played the ball to her.

articles.title: ‘I expect to move forward’: Carrick denies risk of Manchester United sack
articles.summary: ‘Is there?’ manager retorts when told of talk over position. Bizarre 4-4 draw with Villa leaves United in bottom three. A tetchy Michael Carrick dismissed a suggestion he could resign as head coach for the good of the team after Sunday’s chaotic 4-4 draw with Aston Villa left Manchester United in…
body: Carrick’s side sit in 18th place with eight points from 10 games and have won only once, in August at home to Ipswich, in the league this season. It is now a club record eight Premier League games without a win.His job remains in the balance due to the dismal run of form.

Carrick was asked on Sky Sports if he was considering his position. “I’m not,” said the 45-year-old, who was curt when the interviewer said that it was clear there would be conversations regarding his future before United’s next game, which is away to Liverpool on 22 November.

“Is there?” he replied. “You’re telling me. I’m quite clear with what direction the club needs to go in, and it’s got to win games. We haven’t won enough games, but I expect to move forward and keep working on the things that we’ve been working on and showing a lot of the good in the game today, tighten up on a few mistakes and win football matches.”

articles.title: Falkirk add goals and grit to McGlynn's guile on rapid rise
articles.summary: Falkirk continue to excel under the canny guidance of John McGlynn as a run of five successive victories takes them up to third in the Scottish Premiership.
body: In the space of a week Falkirk have beaten defending champions Celtic and become the first team to get the better of Hearts in a Scottish Premiership match at Tynecastle in 19 months, scoring a combined seven goals in the process.
The 5-2 success in Edinburgh was their fifth successive victory and takes John McGlynn's side up to third place.
A month ago, the concession of an added time goal to Dundee left them 11th, only a point off the bottom of the table.
"It's striking a balance without getting carried away and not playing it down too much," McGlynn told BBC Scotland.

articles.title: Hamilton says he overrode Ferrari pit call due to 'lack of information'
articles.summary: Lewis Hamilton says a lack of information led to him overriding Ferrari's call for him to come into the pits as rain fell during the closing stages of the Sao Paulo Grand Prix.
body: Hamilton was running in eighth at Interlagos when heavy rain began to fall with 10 laps to go. While the leaders had already passed the pit entry by the time the rain intensified, Mercedes brought in George Russell from fifth.

Ferrari instructed Hamilton to come in, but he decided to do the opposite to the car just in front of him at the time, Racing Bulls' Liam Lawson. Hamilton's team-mate Charles Leclerc, running just behind him, came into the pits.
The seven-time world champion spun on the next lap in the treacherous conditions, before pitting at the end of it to follow his rivals onto intermediates.

While there was little at stake, as Hamilton ultimately finished ninth rather than claiming what could have been seventh if he had got past Lawson, it was the latest example of imperfect execution from the British driver and his Italia team.

articles.title: Women's TGL: Latest results, schedule as Hull, Woad feature
articles.summary: A look at the fixtures and full schedule for the inaugural women's TGL season, featuring Charley Hull and Lottie Woad, with every match exclusively live on Sky Sports.
body: The tech-infused golf league sees LPGA Tour stars feature in a unique team format, following on from the success of the men's competition, with all players mic'd up and every match being played at SoFi Center - a purpose-built indoor venue in Florida.
Five teams feature in the inaugural season, each having a five-team roster, with Atlanta Drive GC, Boston Common Golf, Los Angeles Golf Club, Motor City Golf Club and New York Golf Club all involved.
Teams play 15 holes of golf each match, divided into two sessions, with nine holes of triples - three against three playing alternate shots - and six holes of head-to-head singles golf.

Each team players four matches in the regular season, with the top four teams in the standings then progressing to the semi-finals. The best-of-three finals then take place on the week beginning December 21, all live on Sky Sports.

articles.summary: Under-pressure Manchester United boss Michael Carrick "expects" to stay on despite his side sitting in the relegation zone after Sunday's dramatic 4-4 home draw against Aston Villa.
body: Man Utd scored twice in stoppage time to rescue an unlikely point against Villa, but the draw leaves Carrick's side third-bottom and a point from safety.
Man Utd's 18th-place position is their lowest after 10 top-flight games since 1986/87, when they were 20th.

The draw against Villa extends Man Utd's winless run in the league to eight games - a club record in the Premier League era - raising further doubts over Carrick's position heading into the two-week November international break.
When questioned on his future by Sky Sports' Patrick Davison, Carrick engaged in a tetchy back-and-forth, insisting he would remain in charge.

articles.title: Inside Greg Luca's AP Top 25 ballot: Alabama, Texas or Tennessee?
articles.summary: Alabama, Texas and Tennessee all have cases to be the top two-loss team from the SEC, and the choice may not be as simple as head-to-head results.
body: Texas beat Tennessee, and Tennessee beat Alabama. So, with all three teams sitting 7-2, just rank them in that order, right?

Well, unfortunately, the answer isn't always so simple, and I'm aligned with my colleagues in the Associated Press Top 25 poll by flouting the head-to-head results, slotting Alabama ahead of Texas and Tennessee, in that order.

Through each week of my debut season with an AP Top 25 ballot, we'll take you inside my thought process behind the picks, starting this week with some of the toughest decisions following the most loaded weekend of the season.

To be clear, Tennessee's 26-10 win against Alabama on Oct. 17 matters quite a bit for the Volunteers' resume. Combined with Saturday's one-sided win against Kentucky, the Alabama win gives Tennessee two quality victories, balanced against losses to Texas and at South Carolina.

articles.title: All-American Sarah Strong’s career-high 39 points powers second-ranked UConn past No. 10 Iowa
articles.summary: Joe Buglewicz/Getty Images. Sarah Strong scored 26 of her career-high 39 points in the first half as No. 2 UConn beat No. 10 Iowa 91-79 on Sunday. Blanca Quinonez had 21 points and hit her fourth 3-pointer of the game with 2:57 remaining after Iowa pulled within 10 points.
body: Chit-Chat Wright had 23 points, Ava Heiden had 15 points and Dani Carnegie finished with 12 points for Iowa (2-1).
Heiden had five points as Iowa jumped out to an early six-point lead. Quinonez came off the bench to score 11 points as UConn finished the first quarter on a 13-3 run.

UConn (2-1) opened the second quarter with 3-pointers by Strong and Ashlynn Shade to take its first double-digit lead. Iowa had the ball late in the second quarter with a chance to go into halftime only down by nine or 10 points. However, a Quinonez steal led to a buzzer-beating 3-pointer from Strong as UConn led 52-37 at the break.

Heiden, Iowa’s top rebounder and third-leading scorer, picked up her second foul with 2:09 left in the first quarter. She didn’t return for the remainder of the first half. The Hawkeyes had one field goal in nearly four minutes when Heiden first went to the bench. Heiden didn’t score in six minutes in the third quarter as she picked up her third and fourth fouls.

Blanca Quinonez had 21 points and hit her fourth 3-pointer of the game with 2:57 remaining after Iowa pulled within 10 points.

articles.title: Michigan fires Jason Beck: Wolverines will owe significant buyout after parting with struggling OC in Year 1
articles.summary: A dismal 15-6 loss to rival Michigan State proved to be the breaking point for a unit ranking near the bottom of the FBS in scoring and total offense
body: Michigan fired offensive coordinator Jason Beck, the school announced on Sunday, one day after a 15-6 loss to Michigan State in which the Wolverines managed only 192 total offensive yards. Offensive line coach Jim Harding will serve as interim offensive coordinator for the remainder of the season.

Beck, the nation's highest-paid offensive coordinator, came with head coach Kyle Whittingham after a successful year together at Utah last season. That success never translated in Ann Arbor, however, on a 5-4 Michigan team that is one of the most disappointing in the country. The loss to Michigan State was the final straw.

"The results have not matched our desired outcome, and I felt that a change in leadership was required for our offense," Whittingham said Sunday. "We need to put our offensive players and the entire team in the best possible position to be successful.

"We appreciate the hard work and effort that Jason has dedicated to the program. Jason is a great man and coach, and unfortunately, it did not work out the way that we wanted it to at Michigan. We wish Jason and his family nothing but the best in the future."
